description: Annexation classified Palestinians in the city as permanent residents. Rights groups describe this as converting an inherent right to live in and enter Jerusalem into a revocable privilege.
energy_note: A birthright, reissued as a licence.

aspect: The rules were changed underneath people
description: Originally residency survived absence of under seven years, and moving elsewhere in the West Bank did not affect it at all. From the mid-1990s the criteria were broadened: moving your 'centre of life' outside Israel - including into the rest of the occupied territory - now costs the status.
energy_note: The goalposts moved, retroactively, for everyone.

description: More than 14,565 Palestinian residencies were revoked between 1967 and 2015.

aspect: Proving your centre of life is a permanent documentary chore
description: Utility bills, school registrations, rent contracts, municipal tax, employer letters - assembled continuously, for years, against the possibility of being asked. The burden of proof sits on the resident.
time_note: Days per year spent maintaining the evidence file.
energy_note: Filing paperwork to prove you live in your own house.

aspect: A second ground was added in 2006: breach of allegiance
description: Since 2006 the Interior Minister has also revoked residency punitively for 'breach of allegiance', which reaches even people who never left the city at all.
energy_note: You can lose it without ever going anywhere.

aspect: It interlocks with the family unification freeze
description: A family awaiting unification must choose: live apart, or have the Jerusalem spouse move out to join the other - which triggers loss of the Jerusalem status under centre-of-life. Leaving also risks the PA refusing them status in the territories.
energy_note: Two policies that catch you between them.

aspect: Rights groups call it forcible transfer
description: HRW argues the revocations effectively force out a population protected under the Fourth Geneva Convention, which permits transfer only temporarily and for imperative military reasons.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the 2006 ground that reaches people who never left
description: Since 2006, in addition to centre-of-life, the Interior Minister has revoked residency punitively for 'breach of allegiance'. This reaches Palestinians who never left Jerusalem at all, so even perfect compliance with the centre-of-life rule is not protective.
energy_note: Doing everything right, and still losing it.
